page.installHintTitle: Add Noise to your Home Screen
page.installHintText: In Safari, tap Share (□↑) and then “Add to Home Screen”. Noise then launches like an app – even without internet.
page.heroText: Free noise generator for white, pink and brown noise – for sleep, focus and winding down. No accounts, no audio files, no tracking.
page.slopeHint: The color presets use approximated spectra; the dB/octave values are guidelines, not a calibrated measurement.
page.rangeHint: Filter cutoff frequencies; outside this range the signal is attenuated, not hard-clipped.
page.presetsHint: Stored on this device only. Clearing browser data may remove presets – back them up as JSON if needed.
page.wavHint: Create a stereo WAV file of your current settings (44.1 kHz / 16 bit). Nothing is uploaded.
page.faqWhiteA: White noise contains all audible frequencies at equal energy. It sounds bright and hissy, like an untuned radio, and masks ambient sounds very evenly.
page.faqPinkA: In pink noise, the energy drops by about 3 dB per octave. That makes it sound warmer and more balanced than white noise – similar to steady rain or wind. Many people find it more pleasant for falling asleep.
page.faqBrownA: Brown noise rolls off even more steeply, by about 6 dB per octave, and sounds deep and muffled, like ocean surf or distant rumbling. It is popular for focus, relaxation and sleep.
page.faqBlueQ: What about blue or violet noise?
page.faqBlueA: Blue (+3 dB/octave) and violet noise (+6 dB/octave) emphasize the high frequencies and sound correspondingly sharp. Use the “Spectral slope” slider to move smoothly between all colors.
page.faqOfflineQ: Does Noise work offline and for free?
page.faqOfflineA: Yes. The noise is generated live in your browser – no audio files are loaded and no data is transmitted. Install Noise as an app on your device and it runs without internet, too.
page.faqNote: Start at a low volume, especially with headphones. Noise is a sound tool, not a medical device.
